questions.q: State what is meant by decomposition.

markPoints.concept: breaking a problem down into smaller problems
markPoints.exemplar: Breaking a problem down into smaller problems.

questions.example: Breaking a large problem down into smaller sub-problems that are easier to solve.
questions.paraphrase: Splitting a big problem into smaller parts.
questions.feedback: Break it into smaller pieces. Abstraction removes detail; decomposition divides the work.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.1 Lesson 2 — Breakdown bay, station 1: What decomposition is

questions.q: Which of these are advantages of decomposing a programming problem? Tick all that apply.
options: Each part is easier to understand and to solve
Different programmers can work on different parts at the same time
A part can be tested on its own
The finished program will always run faster
Less code has to be written in total
correct: Each part is easier to understand and to solve
Different programmers can work on different parts at the same time
A part can be tested on its own
questions.feedback: Decomposition makes a problem manageable. It does not make the program faster or shorter.

questions.q: Explain why decomposition makes a large program easier to test.

markPoints.concept: each part can be tested separately
accept: each part|each piece|every piece|every part|each section|each module|individually|separately|independently|in isolation|on its own|one at a time|each sub
markPoints.exemplar: Each part can be tested separately.

markPoints.concept: so a fault can be traced to the part it is in, rather than searched for in the whole program
markPoints.exemplar: So when a fault appears you know which part it is in.

questions.example: Each sub-problem is solved by its own section of code, which can be tested on its own, so when something goes wrong the fault can be traced to one small part instead of being hunted for across the whole program.
questions.paraphrase: Since every piece can be checked independently, a bug can be pinned down to a single section rather than searched for throughout the entire program.
questions.feedback: Tested separately, therefore faults are findable.
